title: The hypertrophy series: warm up sets impact on tonnage
summary: NH argues warm-up sets are not junk volume: they add tonnage, the heavier ones already fall into relevant intensity windows, and they let you recalibrate technique so later tonnage goes to the target muscle. He rejects rushing warm-ups and tells viewers to program their warm-up jumps deliberately.
claims: Warm-up sets are widely dismissed as junk volume but are much more important than people think
Warm-ups are less hypertrophic than hard sets because they are lighter, mostly outside relevant intensity windows, and done with cold muscles that cannot show true strength
Warm-ups often feel awkward (e.g. 275 lb when top sets are 390), so do not let them psych you out; they are not an indicator of how the work sets will go
Warm-up reps still count toward total tonnage and create some, if minimal, fiber damage
When pyramiding up, sets like 310 lb against a 390 lb rep max are already in a relevant intensity window
Cold muscles make light warm-up weights artificially harder; some claim training cold destroys more fibers, but he would never squat heavy without warming up because tendons and muscles are not ready
Warm-ups let you practice and recalibrate technique, e.g. noticing too much lower back at 135 and fixing it so heavy tonnage goes to the quads
Some argue two one-hour sessions beat one two-hour session partly because you redo warm-up sets, which shows they are not garbage
Don't rush warm-ups like an appetizer; feel the muscles work and move the way you intend
He rejects the powerlifting advice to move warm-ups fast; use the tempo that warms you best and builds confidence, even pausing at three plates to show yourself it is light
Back-off sets often use warm-up weights; fatigue makes them artificially harder, but not enough to call back-offs quality tonnage and warm-ups junk
Program your warm-up jumps week to week; how you load up to your top weight directly affects performance on strength work and progression
exercises: controlled tempo, can pause at 315; use them to fix form before heavy sets
